questions.question: One mole of any substance contains:
Why was Avogadro's number chosen as the size of the mole?
options: It is a perfectly round number
So that one mole of a substance has a mass in grams equal to its relative molecular mass
It matches the number of elements in the periodic table

questions.question: The central formula n = m/M reads in words as:
options: Mass equals moles divided by molar mass
Molar mass equals mass times moles
Moles equal molar mass divided by mass
Moles equal the mass you have divided by the mass of one mole's worth

subtopics.title: Moles from Mass — the 8,8 Gram Question

questions.question: The molar mass of CO2 is:
options: 44 g/mol — carbon 12 plus two oxygens at 16 each

questions.question: The number of moles in 8,8 g of CO2 is:
Which sense check catches an upside-down division here?
options: 8,8 g is one fifth of 44 g, so the answer must be a fifth of a mole — 5 mol would imply 220 g
Answers in chemistry are always whole numbers
Moles must always be greater than 1

subtopics.title: From Moles to Molecules, and to Litres at STP

questions.question: The number of molecules in 0,2 mol of CO2 is:
Avogadro's law states that at the same temperature and pressure:
options: Heavier gases occupy more volume per mole
Equal volumes of any gases contain equal numbers of molecules
Gas volume is independent of the number of molecules

questions.question: The volume of 0,2 mol of CO2 at STP is:
When is the 22,4 dm³/mol molar volume valid?
options: For any substance at any temperature
Only for gases at STP — 273 K and 101,3 kPa

subtopics.title: The Mole Map — Navigating Every Conversion

questions.question: On the mole map, travelling INWARD (from mass, particles or volume to moles) always means:
options: Dividing — by M, by Avogadro's number, or by 22,4 dm³/mol respectively
Using Avogadro's number for every road

questions.question: A question gives a gas volume at STP and asks for its mass. The journey is:
options: Multiply by 22,4, then divide by molar mass
Divide by 22,4 dm³/mol to reach moles, then multiply by the molar mass

questions.question: Computing CO2's molar mass as 28 g/mol comes from which error?
options: Counting the subscripted oxygen only once instead of twice

questions.question: Next term, the coefficients of balanced equations will combine with the mole map to power:
options: The layout of the periodic table
Stoichiometry — converting grams of reactant to grams of product via mole ratios

subtopics.title: Nobody Counts Rice Grains — They Count Bags

questions.question: In the wholesaler comparison, what plays the part of the bag that shops count instead of counting rice grains?
options: The mole — a fixed pack of 6,02 × 10²³ particles

questions.question: Why is the periodic table called the price list, written in grams per pack?
options: It lists the cost of chemicals in rands
It lists how many packs of each element exist
The number printed for an element is the mass in grams of one mole of it
It tells you the volume of one mole

questions.question: Why may weighing stand in for counting particles?
options: Because all particles weigh the same
Because one mole always holds the same number of particles, so a known mass fixes a known count
Because balances can detect single molecules
Because grams and particles are the same unit

subtopics.title: A Fifth of a Bag of Sugar

questions.question: Reading CO2 'like an invoice' — one carbon, two oxygens — gives a molar mass of:
Why must 8,8 g of CO2 come to 0,2 mol before you touch a calculator?
options: Because every gas question gives 0,2 mol
Because 8,8 g is one fifth of the 44 g that one mole weighs, so it is a fifth of a pack
Because moles are always less than 1

questions.question: Going from moles OUT to molecules you multiply, because:
options: Particles are the tiny, numerous thing, so the count must come out enormous

questions.question: 0,2 mol of carbon dioxide contains:

subtopics.title: Same Room for Any Gas — and the Rank in the Middle

questions.question: Why does one mole of any gas fill the same volume at the same temperature and pressure?
options: Because all gases have the same molar mass
Because a gas is mostly empty space — the spacing between particles sets the volume, not the size of each particle
Because gas molecules are all identical in size

questions.question: At STP, 0,2 mol of carbon dioxide occupies:
options: 4,48 dm³ — about two large cooldrink bottles

questions.question: In the taxi-rank picture of the mole map, riding OUT of the rank always means:
options: Multiplying — by the molar mass, by Avogadro's number, or by 22,4 dm³/mol

questions.question: When is the 22,4 dm³/mol shortcut NOT allowed?
options: When the substance is a liquid or a solid, or the gas is not at STP
When the gas is carbon dioxide
When the mass is under 10 g
When the question asks for molecules
